analysis.title: Americas Construction: Building Products: AHRI — September Read-Throughs
key_insights: Residential water heater units fell 3% y/y in September, versus -2% in August and +12% a year ago. Commercial rose 4% y/y versus -5% in August and +15% last year.
Versus 2019, residential water heater units were +8% and commercial +4%. Sequentially residential rose 6% and commercial 16%, after 7% and 18% declines in August.
GS reads the sequential rebound as normalization off weak August demand and pull-forward ahead of AOS's 4-7% price increase that took effect in June.
GS expects ongoing volatility given AOS's December price increase of up to 9.5% and the macro and housing backdrops. It sees possible further pull-forward ahead of the December increase.
GS forecasts a low-single-digit contraction in 2026 residential water heater industry volumes, with AOS residential volumes down 2.7% y/y and commercial up 0.9%.
Residential water heater shipments are down 4% YTD and commercial down 1% YTD. The 2-year stacked 6-month average for residential was down 1% and commercial up 4%.
The residential y/y decline comes against a tough +11.7% comp and weak housing, which GS expects to persist in the coming months.
Residential HVAC shipments were +28% y/y in September, against a -43% comp, and +10% versus 2019 (vs -3% in August). This is the 8th consecutive month of positive data.
Commercial HVAC shipments were +7% y/y in September (vs -12% in September 2025) and +4% versus 2019 (vs -16% in August). Trailing 12-month commercial HVAC was -2%, unchanged from August.

HVAC manufacturers' commentary points to realized 2026 pricing of roughly low-single-digit. GS says easier comps for the rest of the year give further confidence that the bottom is in for residential HVAC shipments.
GS maintains a cautious outlook on AOS, which it rates Sell, on housing moderation, macro uncertainty and shifting comps.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays cautious on AOS on softer housing and macro uncertainty, expecting residential water heater volumes down 2.7% y/y in 2026. Price increases cause pull-forward and volatility. The disclosures list the stock at $64.61.

sector_views.rationale: Residential volumes are expected to contract on weak housing, with volatility around price-driven pull-forward.
Residential HVAC shipments have risen for 8 straight months against easy comps, and GS thinks the bottom is in. Commercial is recovering but is down 2% on a trailing 12-month basis.

earnings_insights: GS estimates AOS residential water heater volumes will contract 2.7% y/y in 2026, with commercial up 0.9% (GS estimate, not reported).
risk_factors: Weak housing demand pressuring residential water heater volumes.
Demand volatility from the AOS December price increase of up to 9.5%, including pull-forward followed by payback.
Broader macro uncertainty and shifting y/y comps.
